content:
PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP & Document AI
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine learning engineer with 5+ years of experience in applied machine learning, natural language processing and document AI. Experienced in taking document classification and NLP models into production, including model serving, production monitoring and cloud deployment on Azure. Strong Python background with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and MLflow. Currently pursuing a PhD focused on named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
- Developed and deployed an incoming-document classifier for public administration documents, achieving 94% accuracy and 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes; the service processes approximately 15,000 documents per day.
- Fine-tuned XLM-R and BERTić transformer models for classification and named entity recognition in Croatian administrative documents.
- Delivered models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service, using Azure ML and MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry.
- Established weekly production monitoring for input text length, vocabulary and predicted class distribution, with alerts when PSI exceeds 0.2. Monitoring identified an OCR change that reduced accuracy by 9 percentage points; the issue was resolved within a week.
- Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 Croatian administrative documents, supported by annotation guidelines and two annotators; achieved inter-annotator Cohen’s kappa of 0.87.
- Mentor two students during their professional internships.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb (remote from Osijek)
09/2021–02/2023
- Developed customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Developed customer complaint topic classification, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic regression baseline to fastText; the 11-topic classification supported weekly reporting to customer service management.
- Prepared SQL reports using the Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava
10/2020–08/2021
- Built a corpus of Croatian legal texts and annotated documents; wrote supporting Python scripts.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
- Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using sentence embeddings, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
- Checked outputs manually; the prototype was not used in production.

EDUCATION
PhD studies in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts | Expected 2027

MSc in Computer Science (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava | 2020

CERTIFICATION
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Azure App Service, Git, Linux, FAISS, sentence-transformers

TEACHING
Guest lecturer, NLP Summer School | 2025 | 90-minute lecture

PUBLICATION
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). “Named entity recognition for Croatian administrative documents.” Workshop on Slavic Language Processing.

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) | English (C1) | German (B2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from research and data science into production machine learning engineering. The strongest content is the quantified production work: 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 23 classes, approximately 15,000 documents per day, a 4,000-document annotated dataset, kappa 0.87, and a documented 9-point accuracy impact from an OCR change. The summary is focused and credible, and the CV appropriately distinguishes the personal RAG prototype from production experience. Education, certification, publication, teaching, languages, and technical skills are presented professionally. The main content limitation is that several relevant tools and the RAG terminology from the candidate's portfolio are not fully surfaced, while some requirements in the advertisement—such as feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, data versioning, CI/CD, and automated testing—are not evidenced in the candidate information and therefore cannot be added truthfully.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard headings, a conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable date formats, explicit technologies, measurable outcomes, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, or unusual formatting. It contains strong matches for Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, Azure ML, MLflow, model serving, monitoring, and named entity recognition. AI screening probability is high for the core production ML, NLP, document AI, Azure, and MLOps-related criteria. ATS matching could be improved by using the exact phrase "retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)" in the project entry and by adding supported tools from the portfolio, including Evidently, Azure Functions, PostgreSQL, Label Studio, and sentence-transformers. The CV should not add unsupported terms such as Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, automated testing, data versioning, feature engineering, or data ingestion pipelines.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the role's production ML, NLP, document-processing, model-serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, and MLflow requirements. The public-administration document classifier and production monitoring work are especially relevant to building and operating AI systems. The personal Croatian-laws question-answering prototype provides truthful exposure to a RAG-style AI product, although it was not used in production and has only manual checking, so it should remain clearly labelled as a prototype. The candidate has a relevant MSc in Computer Science and more than five years of overall machine-learning/data-science experience. However, the available material does not establish at least four full years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer shipping systems to production; the documented ML Engineer role runs from March 2023 to the present. The material also does not show feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, data versioning, CI/CD, automated tests, or orchestration beyond MLflow. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than CV-writing defects and should not be claimed or implied. The CV does not provide evidence about the company's teamwork, ownership, pragmatism, or feedback culture, but this is not a significant defect for the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS and alignment enhancements:
1. In the Selected Projects section under "Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering Demo," change the first bullet to: "Built a weekend retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using sentence embeddings, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API." Keep the existing statement that it was not used in production and was checked manually.
2. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported tools "sentence-transformers, Evidently, Azure Functions, PostgreSQL, Label Studio". These are documented in the candidate portfolio and would improve matching for monitoring, data annotation, and RAG-related screening.
3. In the Machine Learning Engineer experience entry, consider changing "Established weekly production monitoring for input text length, vocabulary and predicted class distribution" to "Established weekly production monitoring for input text length, vocabulary and predicted class distribution using PSI-based alerts". This preserves the existing evidence while making the monitoring methodology more searchable and precise.
